examples.note: Solar output will drop to about 20% from 1 PM to 3 PM.

expected.analysis: Rooftop solar usable output drops to 20% of forecast for two hours in the afternoon.
expected.explanation: Usable solar limited to 20% of forecast for 13:00-15:00.

examples.note: Expect an 80% reduction in rooftop solar between 11 AM and 2 PM due to inverter work.

expected.analysis: Inverter work reduces usable solar by 80% for a three-hour midday window today.
expected.explanation: Usable solar limited to 20% of forecast for 11:00-14:00.

examples.note: Panel washing from one until three will leave roughly one-fifth of normal output.

expected.analysis: Panel washing during early afternoon leaves about one fifth of normal solar output.
expected.explanation: Usable solar limited to 20% of forecast for 13:00-15:00.

examples.note: Haze will cut PV generation by a quarter from 9 AM to noon.

expected.analysis: Haze reduces PV generation by a quarter for a three-hour morning window.
expected.explanation: Usable solar limited to 75% of forecast for 09:00-12:00.

examples.note: Inverter offline 10:00-12:00, so no solar is usable.

expected.analysis: Inverter offline for two hours makes solar completely unusable in that window.
expected.explanation: No usable solar for 10:00-12:00 (inverter offline).

examples.note: Do not charge the battery between 2 PM and 4 PM.

expected.analysis: Charging is explicitly forbidden for a two-hour afternoon window.
expected.explanation: Charging disabled during 14:00-16:00.

examples.note: Charger isolated from 2 AM until 5 AM for maintenance.

expected.analysis: Maintenance isolates the charger overnight, so the battery cannot be charged then.
expected.explanation: Charging disabled during 02:00-05:00 (maintenance).

examples.note: No battery charging after 9 PM.

expected.analysis: Charging is forbidden from 9 PM to the end of the day.
expected.explanation: Charging disabled from 21:00 to end of day.

examples.note: Charging is suspended from 10 PM to 2 AM.

expected.analysis: Charging suspension spans midnight, covering late night and the first two hours of the day.
expected.explanation: Charging disabled 22:00-24:00 and 00:00-02:00.

examples.note: For protection testing, the battery must not discharge from 6 PM until 8 PM.

expected.analysis: Protection testing forbids discharge for a two-hour evening window.
expected.explanation: Discharging disabled during 18:00-20:00 (protection testing).

examples.note: Relay work means the battery cannot feed the campus from 17:00 to 19:00.

expected.analysis: Relay work prevents the battery from supplying the campus for a two-hour window.
expected.explanation: Discharging disabled during 17:00-19:00 (relay work).

examples.note: No discharging from 6 PM through 8 PM.

expected.analysis: Discharge forbidden for a window described with 'through', which is ambiguous at the boundary.

alternative.reason: 'through' can be read as inclusive of the end hour.

expected.explanation: Discharging disabled during 18:00-20:00.

examples.note: Keep at least 120 kWh in reserve from 6 PM until 9 PM.

expected.analysis: The battery must keep at least 120 kWh stored for a three-hour evening window.
expected.explanation: Battery must keep at least 120.0 kWh stored during 18:00-21:00.

examples.note: Hold at least 40% state of charge from 5 PM to 8 PM.

expected.analysis: State of charge must stay at or above 40% of capacity for a three-hour evening window.
expected.explanation: Battery must keep at least 100.0 kWh stored during 17:00-20:00.

examples.note: Keep the battery half full between 7 and 10 in the evening.

expected.analysis: The battery must stay at least half full for a three-hour evening window.
expected.explanation: Battery must keep at least 100.0 kWh stored during 19:00-22:00.

examples.note: Maintain an extra 30 kWh above the usual minimum from midnight to 4 AM.

expected.analysis: The reserve floor is raised 30 kWh above the normal minimum overnight.

quantity.source_text: extra 30 kWh above the usual minimum

expected.explanation: Battery must keep at least 70.0 kWh stored during 00:00-04:00.

examples.note: Keep at least 90 kWh stored all day.

expected.analysis: A 90 kWh reserve floor applies to every hour of the day.
expected.explanation: Battery must keep at least 90.0 kWh stored all day.

expected.analysis: Grid import is capped at 155 kWh per hour for a three-hour evening window.
expected.explanation: Grid import capped at 155.0 kWh per hour during 18:00-21:00.

examples.note: The substation can supply at most 0.18 MWh per hour from 19:00 to 22:00.

expected.analysis: Substation capacity limits grid import to 0.18 MWh per hour for a three-hour window.
expected.explanation: Grid import capped at 180.0 kWh per hour during 19:00-22:00.

examples.note: Grid draw limited to 150 kW for three hours starting at 5 PM.

expected.analysis: Grid draw is capped at 150 kW for a three-hour window beginning at 5 PM.
expected.explanation: Grid import capped at 150.0 kWh per hour during 17:00-20:00.
